In summary, our research is concerned with
the performance analysis of a square array of multiple antennas in the case of SC and MRC, where the correlation of fading signals, angular spread, and one-antenna fault are taken into account.
the performance of SC and MRC over Nakagami correlated fading channels, which is important in the design and implementation of the wireless communication system.
the performance analysis of a square array of antennas with SC and MCR receiver over Nakagamifading channels.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the MRC receiver has better performance than the SC receiver.
the MRC scheme outperforms the SC scheme for the same number of antennas, and that the system performance is degraded in the presence of antenna failure.
the system performance is greatly influenced by both the fading factor and the correlation coefficients, but is less affected by the number of branches.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
MRC outperforms SC in terms of BER performance, and the performance of the system is degraded by correlation and fading.
the performance of MRC is always better than that of SC, and the system with SC is more robust to the failure of antennas.
the square array of four-antenna system is a better choice in the Nakagami correlated environment than the circular array of four antennas.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the square array with SC and/or MRC receiver is more robust to the antenna failure than the linear array.
, in the case of a square array, the system performance with SC is better than that with MRC, especially when the fading factor is large.
the system with MRC receiver is superior to the system with SC receiver, especially in the case of high correlation coefficient.
